A proper-subset witness (\(2r_n>1\)) verifies strict ratio below one. Analytic local Taylor expansions, with explicit even coefficients, prove the two-term asymptotic. Standard-library independent all-disk ray integration checked orders 3,5,7,11 and a numerical expansion test checked 31,51,101. Tests supplement the infinite proof.

Full texts on Groemer–Wallen diameter bisection (2001) and Jin–Guo Minkowski asymmetry (2011), along with Lu–Pan perimeter splits (2005), establish different invariants. Published mathematical-record results for straight regular polygons and for spherical Reuleaux Minkowski asymmetry do not imply the exact Euclidean disk-intersection quotient. Existing current/prior claims include an outer Estermann Reuleaux value and a Reuleaux polar moment, mathematically different. Besicovitch (1951) remains inaccessible; Guo and Jin (2017) explicitly state that Jin (2016) concerns Lu–Pan perimeter asymmetry, although direct 2016 full text was unavailable.

value.rationale: PASS: The Kovner–Besicovitch ratio is an intrinsic affine-invariant central-symmetry area statistic, distinct from chord, perimeter, or outer-hull measures. Its value for the standard full odd Reuleaux family \(n\ge5\) is a natural missing shape descriptor, not an arbitrarily selected numeric case. The result identifies the optimizing centered overlap, gives a closed formula at every natural odd order, and quantifies the leading and next-to-leading loss of symmetry as the shape approaches the disk. The triangle is retained only for consistency with known geometry; value arises from the family-level exact determination.
